Scheme Name: Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT: Post-Doctoral Fellowships (PDF)
Nodal Ministry: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
Details:
The “Post-Doctoral Fellowship (PDF)” is a component of the “Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme for Electronics and IT”, implemented by the Digital India Corporation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, Government of India. The objective of the scheme is to promote R&D, create an innovative ecosystem, and enhance India’s competitiveness in the knowledge-intensive sectors of Electronics System Design & Manufacturing (ESDM) and IT/IT Enabled Services (IT/ITES).
This fellowship is meant for those who have a proven track record as evident from their research publications and recognitions. Support is provisioned for 225 Post-Doctoral Fellowships for candidates for a period of one year, to encourage specialized research in emerging areas.
Benefits:
Nature of Support:
Research Fellowship:
 ₹1.08 Lakh/Month
Contingency Grant:
 ₹1 Lakh for 1 year (on re-imbursement and pro-rata basis depending on the period spent under the award). The claim would be submitted by the awardee through respective institution to PhD Cell in prescribed format.
The fellowship is tenable only in India and can be implemented in any of the recognized & eligible academic and R&D institutions. 
Contingency Grant can be used for minor equipment, consumables and similar items relevant to the research work. The host institution should provide necessary administrative and infrastructural support for the PDF fellow.
There is no provision for providing research personnel support under the scheme. The fellow is expected to undertake the research objectives by himself/herself during the entire duration of the fellowship.
PDF is a full-time assignment. The fellows are not eligible to receive any other fellowship from any Government or Non-Government source during the tenure of the fellowship.
Post-doctoral positions are non-transferrable. The research work is to be carried out in the same eligible institution at which PDF seat is allocated and the fellow is enrolled. 
Duration of Support:
The fellowship is purely a temporary assignment, and is tenable for a period of 1 year.
The award will be for one year initially and extendible based on performance review by PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY.
Eligibility Criteria:
Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme is an institutional scheme wherein eligible institutions submit proposals requesting PDF seats against an active call for proposal by Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme, DIC, MeitY.
1. The call for proposal for PDF seats will be notified by PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY through the web portal https://phd.dic.gov.in/ and/or email. 2. Proposals for allotment of PDF seats are to be submitted by eligible institutions only. Suitable number of seats would be allotted to institutions for further enrollment of PDF fellows on these seats following the scheme guidelines. 3. The institution may design/have its own application form for advertisement of PDF; however, the guidelines for PDF are to be followed which must include the following:
1. The PDF applicant should be an Indian citizen. 1. The PDF applicant must have obtained PhD degree from a recognized University with first class (in terms of grades, etc.) in all preceding levels and a good academic record throughout. 1. The eligible participating institution must ensure that the PDF applicant should have completed PhD within the past 5 years on the last date of submission of application to the institution. 1. The upper age limit for the fellowship is 40 years on the date of submission of application to the eligible participating institution. 1. A suitable Mentor/Guide under whom the proposed research would be carried out, must be identified by the institution. 1. Mentor/Guide of PDF fellow must hold a regular academic/research position in a recognized institution in India. He/she should hold a Ph.D. degree in Science or Engineering. 1. Preference would be given to the PDF applicants who have active industry linkages and their research proposal is directed towards industry specific problems. 1. The research proposal of the PDF applicant, to be submitted to the institution, should define clear objectives, outcomes and deliverables against the award. 1. PDF applicants currently in regular employment will not be considered. However, scientists or researchers with temporary positions in academia or research institutions would be considered however, they would be required to relinquish their current roles if selected for the fellowship. 1. PDF applicants should not have completed their PhD at the same institution where the PDF fellowship is to be awarded. 1. The applicant must have a proven track record as evident from their research publications and recognitions. 1. The applicant should not be availing any other fellowship. ***Discontinuation of the Fellowship*** 1. If any fellow wishes to discontinue the fellowship, the institution should inform PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY immediately. One month’s notice is to be given by the institution before the date of discontinuation. 1. The implementing institution should not incur any expenditure from the date of termination of the award/project or the date of resignation of the fellow. The institution will responsible for submission of work report and other requisite documents. 1. In case the post-doctoral fellow undertakes any full/part-time assignment, his/her PDF award under the scheme would be discontinued. 1. PhD Cell, DIC; MeitY reserves the right to hold/ stop/ discontinue the fellowship at any stage, if - Appropriate progress is not being made. - The grant is not being utilized properly. - Violation/ Non-compliance of guidelines. - Any other reason, which is deemed appropriate by PhD Cell, DIC, MeitY.

Scheme Name: SAKSHAM - KVK 2.0
Details: The scheme "SAKSHAM - KVK 2.0"was launched by the Gujarat Skill Development Mission (GSDM), Labour and Employment Department, Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to provide access to skill development programmes to a wide range of beneficiaries at taluka/village level, enhancing employability and competitiveness in the job market while promoting entrepreneurship. The scheme provides Short-Term Training in National Skills Qualifications Framework Level 1, 2, and 3 courses along with Gujarat Council of Vocational Training courses, and implements Special Projects for marginalized and vulnerable groups. The applicant must be a domicile of Gujarat, looking for fresh skills, reskilling, upskilling opportunities. The scheme is implemented by GSDM through empanelled Implementation Partners across all 33 districts of Gujarat. The applications are accepted online through the GSDM portal.
Benefits:
Training Benefits
Short-Term Training of approximately 300 hours duration in National Skills Qualifications Framework/Gujarat Council of Vocational Training aligned courses.
On-the-Job Training as an integral part of Short-Term Training with duration determined by specific job roles.
Specialized training courses for Special Projects tailored to meet specific needs of marginalized and vulnerable groups.
Training conducted at Saksham Centers established at taluka/village level.
Access to certified Training of Trainers trainers endorsed by respective Sector Skill Councils.
Industry expert and entrepreneur guest lectures on rotational basis.
Assessment and Certification Benefits
Assessment and certification carried out by Sector Skill Councils/Gujarat Council of Vocational Training.
Assessment and certification fees paid directly by Gujarat Skill Development Mission.
Candidates eligible for assessment with minimum 70% attendance for classroom training and 70% for On-the-Job Training.
Employment Support Benefits
Placement assistance and employment opportunities from Implementation Partners.
Multiple placement options including wage employment, probation with stipend/salary, service aggregator portal registration, job work acceptance, self-employment, and apprenticeship opportunities.
Post-placement tracking and support services.
Infrastructure and Facility Benefits
Training centers with basic amenities including drinking water and separate toilets for boys and girls.
Aadhaar-based biometric attendance system and Internet Protocol-based Closed-Circuit Television cameras with Digital Video Recorder systems.
Teaching aids, furniture, fittings, and equipment as per job role requirements.
Conditions
Minimum 70% attendance required for classroom training to be eligible for completion.
Minimum 70% attendance required for On-the-Job Training to be eligible for completion.
Original Aadhaar card verification required during assessment to prevent duplication.
Adherence to batch timings from earliest 7:00 AM to latest 7:00 PM with minimum 4 hours and maximum 8 hours per day training.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be a domicile of Gujarat.
- The applicant must be minimum 14 years of age as per labour law for non-hazardous occupations.
- The applicant must be maximum 59 years of age for Short Term Training.
- The applicant must be maximum 65 years of age for Special Projects.
- The applicant must be looking for fresh skills, reskilling, or upskilling opportunities for Short Term Training.
- The applicant must be out of education, school/college dropout, or unemployed youth for Short Term Training.
- The applicant must belong to marginalized, vulnerable groups requiring special attention or specific job roles for Special Projects.

> ***Eligibility for Special Projects***

The applicant must belong to one of the following categories: _Jail Inmates, Former Prisoners, Juvenile homes, Scheduled Castes, Women, Members of the Transgender Community, Members of the Beggar Community, Senior Citizens and Old age homes, Patients recovered from Mental illness, Children in Shelter Homes and Orphanages, Scheduled Tribes, Economically Backward Communities, Persons with Disabilities, Rural Artisans, or Migrant Workers._

Scheme Name: Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work
Details: The scheme "Documentation of Tiatr through Research Work" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to encourage research work in the field of Tiatr and facilitate writers to take up research work in different aspects of Tiatr, its Song & Music. The scheme provides publication of research work in book form with a minimum of 500 copies printed and remuneration as fixed by TAG as per the researcher's experience. The applicant must be a researcher interested in writing books on tiatr after doing thorough research and must submit three typed copies of the manuscript for approval. The scheme is implemented by the Tiatr Academy of Goa (TAG). The applications for this scheme are accepted offline.
Benefits:
Publication Benefits
TAG will publish the research work in book form after thorough research on the subject.
The publication may be in English or Konkani (Roman Script).
TAG will print a minimum of 500 copies of the book.
100 copies will be given to the writer.
The remaining copies will be used by TAG for various purposes.
Financial Benefits
The author/researcher will be given remuneration as fixed by TAG as per his/her experience for the research work undertaken.
Editorial Support
The manuscript approved by the Recommendation Board shall be edited by a member of Editorial Board.
Editing will include checking for spelling and orthography.
Conditions
*The manuscript received from the author/researcher will be considered for publication only after getting approval from the Recommendation Board appointed by TAG.
*The author/researcher will have to provide TAG, 3 (three) typed copies of the manuscript.
*If approved, the author/researcher will have to submit a soft copy of the manuscript on a Compact Disc/Digital Versatile Disc/pen drive.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be a researcher interested in writing books on tiatr after doing thorough research on the subject.
- Preference will be given to any researcher who has already done research on any aspect of Tiatr, its Song & Music.

Scheme Name: Preservation of Tiatr Literature
Details: The scheme "Preservation of Tiatr Literature" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to preserve the literature related to Tiatr/Khell Tiatr/Khell, their scripts, lyrics of songs (kantaram), music, scripts of one-act plays, and encourage script writers and lyricists to publish their works in book form. The scheme addresses the issue that, although thousands of tiatrs have been produced and staged and songs (kantaram) composed and sung over the decades, not many books of Tiatr/Khell tiatr/Khell/One Act Plays scripts and lyrics of songs (Kantaram) have been published. The scheme provides printing of scripts of tiatrs/khell tiatrs/khells, one-act plays, lyrics of kantaram with or without music in book form in Konkani in Roman Script, and payment of honorarium along with free copies to eligible writers.
Benefits:
Printing Services
Tiatr Academy of Goa will print scripts of tiatrs/khell tiatrs/khells, one-act plays, lyrics of kantaram with or without music in book form in Konkani in Roman Script.
Minimum of 500 copies of each book will be printed.

Category-wise Benefits
Category I (Deceased or Inactive Tiatr Artistes)
One-time honorarium as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa for each tiatr script/anthology of songs.
25 copies of books will be given to the writer or legal heir.
Books will be published by Tiatr Academy of Goa from its funds allotted to the scheme.
Category II (Active Tiatr Artistes)
200 books will be given to the artiste.
One-time honorarium as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa for each tiatr script/anthology of songs.
Books will be published by Tiatr Academy of Goa from its funds allotted to the scheme.
Category III (Individual Artiste/Publisher Self-Publishing)
100% of the cost of printing will be paid by Tiatr Academy of Goa on proper verification of rates.
Must give 100 books to Tiatr Academy of Goa free of cost.
Not entitled for any honorarium from Tiatr Academy of Goa.

Conditions
*The manuscript must adhere to traditional formats as approved by Tiatr Academy of Goa.
*There should not be any adverse remark made in any form either written or verbal against any Governments/Individuals/Institutions or anything against caste, creed and religion in the scripts/lyrics of songs which may hurt the sentiments of anybody.
*If proved to contain adverse remarks, Tiatr Academy of Goa reserves the right not to print the book and refrain from making payment or recall the payment made to the concerned.
Eligibility Criteria:
##### **General Eligibility**
The applicant must be a tiatr artiste or the legal heir of a deceased tiatr artiste.
##### **Category-wise Eligibility**
***Category I:***

- The applicant must be a tiatr artiste who has expired or is living but not active on the tiatr stage.
- The applicant must submit scripts of Tiatr/Khell tiatr/Khell/One Act Plays.
- The applicant must have a minimum collection of 50 songs with or without musical scores if submitting only songs (kantaram).

***Category II:***

- The applicant must be a tiatr artist who is active on the tiatr stage.
- The applicant must submit scripts of Tiatr/Khell tiatr/Khell/One Act Plays.
- The applicant must have a minimum collection of 100 songs with or without musical scores if submitting only songs (kantaram).

***Category III:***

- The applicant must be an individual artist/publisher who wishes to publish Scripts of Tiatr/Khell tiatr/Khell/One Act Plays on his/her own.
- The applicant must ensure the book conforms to all norms of the scheme.

##### ***Preference***
Scripts/lyrics/music written by tiatr artistes of yesteryears will be given first preference.

Scheme Name: Craftsmen Training Scheme
Nodal Ministry: Ministry Of Skill Development And Entrepreneurship
Details: The "Craftsmen Training Scheme" was launched by the Directorate General of Training, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India. The scheme aims to ensure a steady flow of skilled workers in different trades for the domestic industry, to raise quantitatively and qualitatively the industrial production by systematic training, to reduce unemployment among the educated youth by providing them with employable skills, and to cultivate and nurture a technical and industrial attitude in the minds of the younger generation. The scheme provides systematic vocational training through a network of Industrial Training Institutes and National Skill Training Institutes located all over the country, offering comprehensive skill development programs in various trades and conducting All India Trade Tests for certification.
Benefits:
Vocational Training and Skill Development
Training Duration:
 Varies from 6 months to 2 years, depending on the trade.
Trade Certification:
 National Council for Vocational Training certificate upon successful completion.
Skill Development:
 Hands-on practical training in various industrial trades.
Employment Opportunities:
 Enhanced employability in domestic and international markets.
Training Infrastructure and Facilities
Training Network:
 Access to 15,042 Industrial Training Institutes and 33 National Skill Training Institutes.
Modern Equipment:
 Training on the latest industrial equipment and technology.
Expert Instruction:
 Training by qualified instructors and industry experts.
Workshop Facilities:
 Well-equipped workshops for practical training.
Assessment and Certification
All India Trade Tests:
 Conducted by the Directorate General of Training under the aegis of the National Council for Vocational Training at the end of training.
National Recognition:
 Certificates recognized across India for employment.
Industry Standards:
 Training aligned with current industry requirements and standards.
Conditions
Minimum 80% attendance is required to appear in the Final Trade Test.
Regular participation in practical training sessions and workshops.
Compliance with the institute rules and regulations.
Successful completion of periodic assessments and tests.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be an Indian citizen.
- The applicant must meet the age requirements as specified for different trades (generally between 14 to 40 years).
- The applicant must have completed the minimum educational qualifications as prescribed for specific trades (ranging from 8th standard to 12th standard).
- The applicant must be able to read and write in the local language / Hindi / English.
- The applicant must be physically and medically fit to undergo the specific trade training.
- The applicant must not have any physical disabilities that would prevent them from performing the trade activities.
- The applicant must meet specific requirements for certain trades (such as color vision for electrical trades).
- The applicant must demonstrate basic aptitude for the chosen trade.

Details:

Through this scheme, financial support is provided to fishermen and related beneficiaries for constructing ice plants or storage units with a minimum capacity of 30 tonnes, ensuring hygienic fish storage and better returns. The scheme is implemented by the Commissioner of Fisheries of the State Governments, with 60% contribution from the Government of India and 40% contribution from the State Government. > **Objective of the scheme**


- Marine production in the Gujarat state is one of the leading in the country. The state lags behind in exports due to non-norms. So cold storage/ice plant modernization is necessary to keep the fish in healthy condition.
- Insulated vehicle, three wheeler with ice box including e-rickshaw, and live fish vending center to deliver the fish in hygienic condition to the consumer, so that the consumer (customer) can get fresh and clean fish from the local area and get good returns to the sellers.
- Around 27,000 small and large boats are operating in the state. To strengthen the safety and security of the fishermen and increase the income of the boat owner, replacement of the existing boats is necessary to increase the sea growth of the existing boats.
Benefits:
Establishment of Open Sea Cages (100-120 m³ volume):
The estimated unit cost is ₹5,00,000/- for the general category against ₹(Rs.) 40% assistance, i.e., ₹2,00,000/- or 40% of the purchase (whichever is less). 
60% contribution of the central government and 40% of the state government will be in the assistance received.
1 Sea-Cage unit under this scheme against the estimated unit cost of ₹ 5,00,00,000/- for women/SC/ST. 60% assistance for the category, i.e. assistance of ₹ 3,00,000/- or 60 % of the actual purchase, whichever is less, is available to the beneficiary.
60% contribution of the central government and 40% of the state government will be in the assistance received. The benefit will be available as per the target (category) allocated by the Government of India.

Remarks: 
60% contribution from Government of India and 40% contribution from State Governments is paid.
Minimum Time Limit (in Years) for Reclaiming Benefits: 
Once in a lifetime.
Eligibility Criteria:
1. The applicant should be a native of Gujarat state.
1. The applicant should have a fishing boat registered under Real Craft software.
1. The applicant should hold a fishing license.
1. The applicant should complete the online registration on the [iKhedut Portal](https://ikhedut.gujarat.gov.in/site/).1. The applicant should obtain in-principle approval before purchase of the floor plan.
1. The applicant should have his/her own bank account.

> **Preference/Reservation/Relaxation:**



  - Women, SC, and ST beneficiaries are eligible for 60% assistance of the unit cost.
  - General category beneficiaries are eligible for 40% assistance of the unit cost.

  - Have one or both parents deceased, or
  - Are children with disabilities, or
  - Are ragpickers, beggars, or from urban deprived and weaker sections.

Scheme Name: Visit to Old/Sick Artistes
Details: The scheme "Visit to Old/Sick Artistes" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to make our younger generation aware of the contribution and sacrifices of Tiatr artistes of yesteryears. TAG has observed that many veteran tiatr artistes who have contributed to the development of tiatr immensely in the past, today have become old, and often pass their time in sickness/loneliness. Therefore, TAG has formulated this scheme so that occasional visits to these veteran artistes will make them feel that TAG cares for them during their old age.
Benefits:
Members of tiatr fraternity will visit these sick/old artistes at their residences or if admitted, visit the hospital and inquire about their health.
TAG will provide the vehicle or travelling allowance to travel and refreshments/working meal to the members who volunteer to visit the old/sick artistes.
During the first visit of this nature, one-time financial assistance of Rs. 10,000/- (or as fixed by TAG) by cheque will be gifted to the artiste which he/she can use for his/her medical expenses.
Eligibility Criteria:
1. TAG will identify the sick/old tiatr artistes based on reports from the fraternity.
2. The artistes who have contributed at least 10 years towards tiatr (Commercial or Non-commercial) /khell tiatr/ khell or the writer/director who has staged at least 10 tiatrs (Commercial or Non-commercial) /khell tiatr/ khell will be eligible.
3. Members of tiatr fraternity must visit these sick/old artistes at their residences or if admitted, visit the hospital and inquire about their health.

Scheme Name: Lifetime Contribution to Tiatr Awards (Commercial)
Details: The scheme "Lifetime Contribution to Tiatr Awards (Commercial)" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to recognize and honor tiatr artistes who have contributed immensely for the development of tiatr, its song and music in the past, addressing the need to acknowledge their lifetime dedication to this traditional art form. The scheme provides a comprehensive recognition package including a shawl, memento, citation, and cash award as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa, along with the prestige of being honored at a special function held annually on 14th December on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of Joao Agostinho Fernandes, 'The Father of Tiatr'. The applicant must be not less than 60 years of age (with health-based relaxation provision) and must have at least 20 years of contribution in the field of tiatr with specific performance requirements based on their role. The scheme is implemented by Tiatr Academy of Goa. The applications for this scheme are accepted through recommendations from individuals/institutions and advertisements in local newspapers.
Benefits:
Award Components:
 Shawl, memento, citation, and cash award as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa
Special Recognition Ceremony:
 Honored at a special function organized on 14th December every year on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of Joao Agostinho Fernandes, 'The Father of Tiatr'
Annual Limit:
 Not more than 5 artistes from the field will be conferred with awards every year
Exclusivity:
 Award conferred only once in a lifetime across all categories (Commercial/Non-Commercial Tiatr, Khell, Khell-Tiatr, or Konkani Cinema)
*The selected artiste must be compulsorily present in person to receive the award.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be not less than 60 years of age.
- The applicant must have at least 20 years of contribution in the field of tiatr.
- The applicant, if an actor/singer/Stage Manager/Lights provider/Make-up artist/Costume designer/Live Music/Background music provider/organizer/contractor, must have performed in at least 30 tiatrs.
- The applicant, if a writer/director, must have written/directed at least 20 tiatrs.
- *The age limit of 60 years may be relaxed if the health of the artist is not well.

##### ***Assessment Criteria***
The applicant's excellence as an actor, script writer, director, singer, lyricist, set designer will be considered.
The applicant's receipt of any awards in their field will be evaluated.
The applicant's innovations on the tiatr stage will be assessed.
The applicant's songs (kantaram) recorded on records, cassettes, CDs/DVDs or online will be considered (if singer/musician).
The applicant's work in dramas in other languages or films besides tiatr will be evaluated.
The applicant's published books of scripts/lyrics will be considered (if script writer or lyricist).
##### ***Post-Selection Conditions***
The applicant must be compulsorily present in person to receive the award.

Scheme Name: Right to Education Act 2009 - Uttarakhand
Details: The “Right to Education Act 2009” is implemented under the Samagra Shiksha Programme by the Secondary Education Department, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide free education, textbooks, uniforms, and the benefits of the PM Poshan Yojana to children up to Class 8 in private schools, targeting rural and urban children from weaker and deprived sections of Uttarakhand.
Benefits:
Under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act, children from weaker and disadvantaged sections in rural and urban areas of Uttarakhand are provided free education, textbooks, uniforms, and the benefits of the PM Poshan Yojana up to Class 8 in private schools.
In private schools, 25% of the total seats in the entry-level class are reserved for children from weaker and disadvantaged sections under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right to Education Act.
Eligibility Criteria:
**Children from the following categories will be eligible for admission up to Class 8 in private schools:**

   1. **Children from weaker sections:** Those whose parents/guardians have an annual income of ₹55,000/- or less, or are BPL card holders.   1. **Children from disadvantaged classes:** SC, ST, and children belonging to the non-creamy layer of OBC, with a family annual income of up to ₹4.5 lakh.   1. Orphan children.
   1. Children with physical disabilities.
   1. Children living with HIV/AIDS or those dependent on parents who are HIV/AIDS positive.
   1. Children dependent on disabled parents or parents affected by leprosy, with a family annual income of less than ₹4.5 lakh.
   1. Children dependent on a divorced or widowed mother, with an annual family income of less than ₹80,000/-.

Scheme Name: Soil Health Card Scheme - Uttarakhand
Details: The scheme “Soil Health Card Scheme” is implemented by the Department of Agriculture, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide Soil Health Cards to all farmers in the state, helping them understand the nutrient composition of their soil and the type and quantity of fertilizers suitable for their crops.
Benefits:
To provide Soil Health Cards to all farmers in the state.
The soil of each farmer’s field is tested at soil testing laboratories, which are operational in all 13 districts.
Farmers receive detailed information about the nutrient content of their soil, along with recommendations on the type and quantity of fertilizers best suited for their crops.
Soil testing is provided free of cost to farmers.
In hilly areas, a Soil Health Card is issued for agricultural land up to 2.5 hectares, while in plain areas, it is issued for land up to 10 hectares. Each card is valid for three years.
Eligibility Criteria:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be a farmer.
1. The farmer must own agricultural land in the state and be actively engaged in farming activities.

Scheme Name: Production of Tiatr in Villages/Urban Areas/Educational Institutions
Details: The scheme "Production of Tiatr in Villages/Urban Areas/Educational Institutions" by the Tiatr Academy of Goa under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa, aims to explore hidden singing and acting talents among the youths in villages and provide encouragement to develop such talents by promoting tiatr activities among villagers, addressing the need to nurture local artistic capabilities in rural and urban areas including educational institutions. The scheme provides financial and technical support for various aspects including direction, live band, outside artistes, stage setting, background music, costumes, make-up, and light effects, along with technical guidance through directors from Tiatr Academy of Goa's Panel of Directors.
Benefits:
Financial Support:
 Tiatr Academy of Goa will provide financial support to the extent as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa towards various aspects: Direction, Live Band (with at least 2 blowing instruments), Outside Artistes, Stage Setting, Background Music, Costumes, Make-up, Light Effects.
Technical Guidance:
 Provision of director from Tiatr Academy of Goa's Panel of Directors who will direct village talents and produce the tiatr.
Director Expenses:
 The expenditure incurred in engaging the director will be borne by Tiatr Academy of Goa.
Marketing Materials:
 Provision of one banner which should be compulsorily displayed on one of the two front side wings of the stage.
Documentation:
 Tiatr Academy of Goa may video film the performance at Kala Academy.
Observer Support:
 Tiatr Academy of Goa may depute an observer from its Panel of Observers to see whether the performance has been made as per the norms of the scheme.
Payment Method:
 Payment will be made directly to the service providers.
Sponsorship Policy:
 Sponsorship from businessmen, firms etc. may be taken.

Conditions
*The performance of the tiatr should be staged in the village/urban area of production.
*The tiatr should be shown to the people free without charging any tickets.
*Submit statement of expenditure enclosing all original bills (stamped receipt if the amount exceeds ₹5,000/-).
*Provide 20 invitation cards/entry passes to Tiatr Academy of Goa well in advance from the middle of rows A, B, or C.
*Return banner to Tiatr Academy of Goa after the show is staged.
*Payment will be made only after the receipt of the observer's certificate.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be an Educational Institution, Cultural Association, Dramatic Troupe, or Individual.
- The applicant must be interested in promoting Tiatr culture in the village.
- The applicant must be from the particular village/urban area/parish (in case of Mumbai, Sindhudurg and other parts of the country).
- The participating artistes must be from the particular village/urban area/parish (Educational Institutions only).
- A maximum of 3 artistes from outside the village/urban areas/parish must be allowed to act as well as sing in the tiatr.
- The tiatr must be produced in its original format including 6 or 7 acts (podd'dde) with at least 4 'cantos' and comedy linked to the story of the play.
- The tiatr must include at least 14 'Kantaram' which includes at least 2 Duets, 1 Duo, 2 Trios, 1 Quartet/Quintet, 2 Choral Songs and Solos.
- The applicant must not make any adverse remark in any form either written or verbal against any Governments/Individuals/Institutions or anything against caste, creed and religion in the scripts/lyrics of songs/performances/speeches which may hurt the sentiments of anybody.
- The applicant must communicate the schedule of practices to Tiatr Academy of Goa well in advance.
- The applicant must discuss with Tiatr Academy of Goa and decide who will be the Chief Guest/Guest of Honour at the performance well in advance.
- The applicant must ensure this is the first performance of the tiatr for which financial assistance is sought from Tiatr Academy of Goa. ***Script and Performance Requirements***

- The script and songs may be written/composed by anyone from within the village or elsewhere but acting and singing must be done by the artistes from the particular village/urban area/parish.
- Musicians may be from anywhere and not necessarily from the village.
- Advertising Requirements: In all advertisements, oral, or print or electronic media, banners, etc. the following must be inserted/published/announced 'This Tiatr is organized in collaboration with Tiatr Academy of Goa'.

Details: The scheme "Promotion of Duets/Duos/Trios/Quartets/Quintets/Choral Songs" was launched by the Tiatr Academy of Goa. The scheme aims to preserve the traditional concept of singing of duets/duos/trios/quartets/quintets/choral songs, which has been on the decline, and to ensure that the correct concept as done traditionally by the tiatr stage artistes of yesteryears is followed. Best Duet: 1st Prize - ₹3,000/-, 2nd Prize - ₹1,500/-.
Best Duo: 1st Prize - ₹3,000/-, 2nd Prize - ₹1,500/-.
Best Trio: 1st Prize - ₹4,500/-, 2nd Prize - ₹2,250/-.

Best Choral Song: 1st Prize - ₹2,000/- to ₹4,000/- (maximum 4 participants), 2nd Prize - ₹1,000/- to ₹2,000/- (maximum 4 participants).

Scheme Name: Samriddhi – Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe Students for Setting Start-Ups
Details: The scheme "Samriddhi – Scheme for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe Students for Setting Start-Ups" was launched by the All India Council for Technical Education. The scheme aims to provide opportunities for Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe students to design, launch, and run their own business or startup after formal education is completed or during their final year of education. The scheme provides a limited one-time financial assistance of ₹20,00,000/- (of which ₹1,00,000/- per year is a recurring grant) to the institute, which then selects nine registered startups of Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe students and provides ₹2,00,000/- seed money to each startup.
Benefits:
Total funding provided is ₹20,00,000/-.
Limited one-time financial assistance of ₹20,00,000/- is provided to the Institute.
Seed money of ₹2,00,000/- per startup will be given, and this amount is non-refundable.
Funding is allocated for nine startups of Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe students.
₹2,00,000/- will be given to the institute specifically for meeting the expenditure associated with the selection procedure.
₹1,00,000/- per year shall constitute a recurring grant portion of the total funding.
Other Details
The total duration of the Scheme shall be for a period of 2 years.
100% of non-recurring funds are released at the time of the award of the scheme.
₹1,00,000/- each is released as recurring funding for two consecutive years.
The seed money is provided to passed out or present students for starting their own enterprise after completion of the formal education from the same institute.
Conditions
The Institute must set up a committee to select nine already registered startups of Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe students.
It is essential that the center has dedicated faculty serving as the Principal Coordinator and dedicated support staff to ensure smooth functioning and effective meeting of its objectives.
The Institute must devise a feedback mechanism to assess the importance of the program.
Feedback shall be obtained after each program from each of the beneficiaries.
If deemed necessary based on feedback, the Institute can update its curriculum for these programs.
Exclusions from Benefit
Startup beneficiaries who are already receiving benefits from other schemes of the All India Council for Technical Education or the Government of India will not be entitled to this scheme.

- The applicant (Institute/University Department) must have been in existence for a period of at least 10 years.
- The applicant (Institution) must possess a good incubation center.
- The incubation center's activities must have been happening for at least 5 years.
- The applicant (Institute) must have a minimum of 50 Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe students enrolled on average during the last 3 years.
- The applicant (Institute) must comply with the guidelines of the Tribal Sub Plan and the Scheduled Caste Sub Plan of the Government of India.
- Student Eligibility (For selection by the Institute)
- The applicant (Student) must be in the final year of their degree or diploma course.
- The applicant (Student) must have a registered company or startup in their name.

Scheme Name: AVYAY - National Action Plan for Senior Citizens: Health and Shelter for Senior Citizens
Nodal Ministry: Ministry Of Social Justice and Empowerment
Details: The scheme "AVYAY - National Action Plan for Senior Citizens: Health and Shelter for Senior Citizens" was launched by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Govt. of India. The scheme is a component of the umbrella scheme " Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY)". The scheme aims to improve the quality of life of Senior Citizens, particularly those who are indigent, by providing basic amenities like shelter, food, medical care and entertainment opportunities. The scheme provides financial assistance for projects such as the maintenance of Senior Citizen Homes (popularly known as Old Age Homes), Continuous Care Homes, Regional Resource and Training Centres (RRTCs), Mobile Medicare Units, and Physiotherapy Clinics under its two sub-schemes: the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) and the State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC).
Benefits:
Grant-in-Aid (GIA) for Senior Citizen Homes (25 beneficiaries)
Annual recurring expenditure grants are provided based on the classification of the city (X, Y, or Z), ranging from ₹25,04,355/- (X Category) to ₹24,38,355/- (Z Category).
Grant-in-Aid (GIA) for Senior Citizen Homes (50 beneficiaries/50 elderly women only)
Annual recurring expenditure grants range from ₹42,11,228/- (X Category) to ₹41,12,228/- (Z Category).
Grant-in-Aid (GIA) for Continuous Care Homes (minimum 20 beneficiaries)
Annual recurring expenditure grants range from ₹30,77,310/- (X Category) to ₹30,11,310/- (Z Category).
Non-Recurring Grant for Senior Citizen Homes (25 indigent)
A grant of ₹3,09,105/- is admissible every five years, which includes the cost of Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras and website development charges.
Non-Recurring Grant for Senior Citizen Homes (50 indigent)
A grant of ₹4,12,140/- is admissible every five years.
Non-Recurring Grant for Continuous Care Homes (20 indigent)
A grant of ₹3,09,105/- is admissible every five years.
Funeral Expenses
Reimbursement of funeral expenses is provided at ₹10,000/- per person or the actual expenses incurred, whichever is less, in case of the demise of any inmate.
State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) Funding
Financial support equivalent to 90% of the project cost is provided for admissible programmes proposed under State Action Plans.

Disbursal Mode, Frequency, and Conditions
Grant-in-aid is provided through the E-anudaan portal and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS)/Expenditure, Audit and Tender (EAT) module.
The total annual grant is released in two equal half-yearly instalments.
Conditions for Disbursement
Recurring Grant-in-aid for Senior Citizen Homes is based on the number of days of attendance of beneficiaries as recorded through a contactless Information Technology (IT) system.
The second half-yearly instalment is released only after the inspection report of the State Government, the officers of the Central Ministry, or the Project Monitoring Unit (PMU) is received.
Conditions for Continuation
Implementing Agencies must maintain the standards laid down in the scheme guidelines.
Implementing Agencies must use the Expenditure, Audit and Tender (EAT) module of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
Implementing Agencies must provide live streaming of the institution's functioning via Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) cameras on their websites/E-anudaan website.
The assistance provided is subject to the Implementing Agency maintaining the institution in the manner prescribed in the guidelines and standards.
Eligibility Criteria:
##### ***For Senior Citizens***
1.  The applicant must be a Senior Citizen.
2.  The applicant must be one of the following:

- Indigent, having no sufficient means to maintain himself/herself, as determined by the State Government.
- Afflicted with Alzheimer's disease/Dementia or seriously ill requiring continuous nursing care, for admittance into Continuous Care Homes.

##### ***For Implementing Agencies (General)***
1.  The applicant must be one of the following:

- State/Union Territory Government.
- Panchayati Raj Institution (PRI).
- Urban Local Body (ULB).
- An Institution or Organization set up by the Government as autonomous/subordinate bodies.
- A Government Recognized Educational Institution.
- A recognized youth organization such as Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS).

##### ***For Implementing Agencies (Non-Governmental Organizations/Voluntary Organizations)***
1.  The applicant must be registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (XXI of 1860) or any relevant Act of the State/Union Territory.
2.  The applicant must be one of the following:

- A Public Trust registered under the law for the time being in force.
- A charitable company licensed under Section 25 of the Companies Act, 1958.
- Indian Red Cross Society or its branches.
- Any other public body or institution having a legal status of its own.
- Any other organization of repute, which may be approved by the Secretary, Department of Social Justice and Empowerment.

3.  The applicant (Voluntary Organization) should have been registered for at least two years.
4.  The applicant should have had at least two years' experience in the social sector at the time of applying for the grant.
5.  The applicant must have a Bank Account maintained and operated in the joint name of the Non-Governmental Organization/Voluntary Organization.
6.  The applicant (for Continuous Care Homes) must have shown a credible track record in running Charitable Hospitals/Nursing Homes/Medical Institutions/Colleges.
##### ***Preference/Priority***
The applicant agency will be selected in the order of preference as follows: Self Help Groups of the senior citizens, Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Foundations/Charities already in the field of elderly care, Start-ups in the segment of elderly care, and Non-Governmental Organizations/Trusts operating in the elderly care segment.

Scheme Name: Assistance for Completely Damaged/Destroyed Houses
Details: The scheme “Assistance for Completely Damaged/Destroyed Houses” is implemented by the Uttarakhand State Disaster Management Authority under the Department of Disaster Management, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to individuals whose residential houses have been completely or partially damaged due to natural disasters in Uttarakhand.
Benefits:
Under this scheme, the following assistance is provided:
Pucca house, Kutcha house, severely damaged/destroyed house, or partially damaged/destroyed house: ₹1,20,000/- per house in plain areas.
For hilly areas (including districts covered under the Integrated Action Plan): ₹1,30,000/- per house.
Pucca house (other than hut) with at least 15% damage: ₹6,500/- per house.
Kutcha house (other than hut) with at least 15% damage: ₹4,000/- per house.
Damaged/destroyed hut: ₹8,000/- per hut. (A “hut” means a temporary, transferable, and below-grade unit constructed with materials such as thatch, mud, or plastic, and is traditionally recognised as a hut by the State/District Administration.) Note: The damaged house must be verified as an authorised construction by the competent authority of the State Government.
Cattle shed attached to the house: ₹3,000/- per cattle shed.
Eligibility Criteria:
1. The applicant must be a resident of Uttarakhand.
1. The applicant must be the owner of a disaster-affected house.

Scheme Name: Vidhyadeep Yojana
Details: The scheme “Vidhyadeep Yojana” was launched by the Education Department, Government of Gujarat. The scheme aims to provide insurance cover to students studying in primary, secondary, and higher secondary schools in the State. The scheme provides maximum financial assistance up to ₹50,000/- per student in case of accidental death or permanent total disability. The scheme is implemented by the State Insurance Fund (Directorate of Insurance) or private/public sector general insurance companies. The applications for this scheme are accepted by the Office of the District Primary Education Officer / District Education Officer / Administrative Officer (through the Principal of the school concerned).
Benefits:
Accidental Death
₹50,000/- per student.
Accidental Permanent Disability
In case of loss of two eyes or both limbs or arm/leg due to accident: ₹50,000/-.
In case of loss of one eye and one limb due to accident: ₹50,000/-.
In case of loss of one eye or one limb due to accident: ₹25,000/-.
Conditions
The incident must be unexpected, sudden, and unintentional, and show visible signs of external violence.
The claim application must be submitted to the Nodal Officer within ninety (90) days from the date of the accident or death.
The benefit amount must not be paid for more than one category if the beneficiary is covered under multiple categories of the overall scheme.
Eligibility Criteria:
> ***For the Student Beneficiary***


- The beneficiary must be a student studying in all Primary, Secondary, and Higher Secondary schools of Gujarat.

> ***For the Applicant/Claimant***


- The applicant must be the successor or the disabled beneficiary themselves in case of permanent disability.
- The applicant must appear in person with the original identity card.
- The applicant must submit the written application in the prescribed format to the local Nodal/Competent Officer.
- The application must be submitted within ninety (90) days from the date of death or accident.

Scheme Name: CM-Vashistha Guru Puraskar
Details: The scheme “CM-Vashistha Guru Puraskar” was launched by the Directorate of Education, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to celebrate the unique contribution of some of the finest teachers in the state and to honour those teachers who through their commitment and industry have not only improved the quality of school education but also enriched the lives of their students. The scheme provides State Awards to Teachers, with each award consisting of a cash amount of ₹1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh) and a citation.
Benefits:
Cash Award:
 ₹1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh).
Citation:
 Provided with each award.
Total 10 Awards:
Primary Teacher: Two Awards (One in each District).
Secondary Teacher: Four Awards (Two in each District).
High School Headmaster: Two Awards (One in each District).
Higher Secondary Teacher: One Award (One in entire State).
Higher Secondary Principal: One Award (One in entire State).
*The recipients will be felicitated at the hands of the Chief Minister of Goa during the Teacher’s Day function.
*The selected teachers will have to make a presentation before the State Level Committee.
Eligibility Criteria:
***Target Group Definition***
    ◦ The applicant must be a school teacher, special educator, or Head of School.
    ◦ The applicant must be working in a recognized government or aided primary, middle, high, or higher secondary school.
    ◦ The applicant must be an in-service teacher.
    ◦ The applicant must fulfill the required academic and professional qualifications as per their cadre for the State Award to Teachers.
***Service Requirements***
    ◦ The applicant, if an in-service Regular Teacher or Special Educator, must have completed at least 15 years of regular teaching service in the State of Goa as on June 30th of the academic year for which they are applying.
    ◦ The applicant, if a Headmaster, must have 5 years of administrative experience out of the required 15 years of regular teaching service in the State of Goa.
***Preference/Reservation***
    ◦ One award out of the 10 is reserved for a differently abled teacher or Head of the School/Special Educator from Regular or Special Schools.
    ◦ The applicant applying for the Differently Abled Category must attach a disability certificate indicating more than 40% disability.

Scheme Name: Young Achievers Awards
Details: The scheme "Young Achievers Awards" was launched by the Tiatr Academy under the Art, Culture and Museums Department, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to recognize young talented artistes who have contributed and continue to work for the development of tiatr, its song and music, and have enriched Konkani Tiatr and Song through All India Radio, Doordarshan and other platforms at national and international levels. The scheme provides recognition through awards consisting of a memento, citation and cash burse, given to one male and one female artiste annually. The scheme also provides a special honour function held on 16th November on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of Regina Fernandes, the First Lady of the Tiatr Stage.
Benefits:
Award Components:
 The Young Achievers Award consists of a memento, a Citation and a Cash Burse as fixed by Tiatr Academy of Goa.
Recognition Ceremony:
 Selected artistes are honoured at a special function on 16th November on the occasion of the Birth Anniversary of Regina Fernandes, the First Lady of the Tiatr Stage.
Annual Awards:
 The award is given to a male and a female artiste every year.
*The selected artistes must be compulsorily present in person to receive the award.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be not more than 35 years of age.
- The applicant must have contributed in the field of tiatr for at least 10 years.
- The applicant must have performed in at least 15 tiatrs.
- The applicant's contribution should be considered in areas such as acting, script writing, directing, singing, lyricist work, set designing, etc.

***Relaxation***
The age limit may be relaxed if the health of the artiste is not well. ***Selection Criteria***

- The applicant's contribution as an actor, script writer, director, singer, lyricist, set designer, etc.
- The applicant should have received or won any awards in his/her field.
- The applicant should have done any innovation on the tiatr stage.
- The applicant, if a singer/musician, should have songs recorded on Compact Discs, Digital Versatile Discs, All India Radio, Doordarshan, online, etc.
- The applicant should have acted/directed/sung/composed music/composed lyrics/designed sets/provided background music/designed light effects for dramas in other languages or in films.
- The applicant, if script writer or lyricist, should have published any books of his/her scripts/lyrics.
- The applicant, if a writer/director, should have written/directed at least 7 tiatrs.
- The applicant's contribution in acting/singing/providing live music/stage setting/background music, providing lights, as a makeup artiste should be at least for 10 years and should have performed in at least 15 tiatrs.

Details: The “Goa State Logistics and Warehousing Incentives Scheme” was launched by the Department of Industries, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to provide financial assistance for the development of the logistics and warehousing industry in the State. The “Subsidy towards Investment of Fixed Capital” component of the scheme offers a capital subsidy rate of 10% or 15% (for special categories) of fixed capital invested in Fixed Assets, capped between ₹25,00,000/- to ₹50,00,000/- per unit per year, depending on the project category and location. The scheme is implemented by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce. The applications for this scheme are accepted through the Goa Online Portal.
Benefits:
Standard Projects
Eligible entities (Logistics Parks (Multi-modal/Integrated), Inland Container Depots, Container Freight Stations, Air Freight Stations, Warehouses, Cold Chain Units, Testing Facilities, Truck Terminals) are entitled to 10% of fixed capital invested in Fixed Assets.
Maximum Amount:
 Capped at ₹25,00,000/- per unit per year.
Special Category Projects
Eligible entities (Projects constructed in Backward Talukas OR owned by Women Entrepreneurs/Entrepreneurs belonging to Schedule Caste/Schedule Tribe Communities) are entitled to 15% of fixed capital invested in Fixed Assets.
Maximum Amount:
 Capped at ₹50,00,000/- per unit per year.
Benefit Disbursal Criteria/Conditions
Mode and Frequency:
 The processing of the application and the disbursement of the incentive amount must be completed within a maximum period of 90 days from the date of application received. Disbursement is performed by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce (DITC).
Time/Chronology:
 All sanctioned claims will be organized chronologically and disbursed to the respective entities following due procedure.
Sanction Basis:
 The subsidy shall be sanctioned to aided entities within the project cost approved by the Financial Institution and an empanelled Chartered Accountant.
Employment Criteria:
 The quantum of benefit sanctioned is determined by the proportion of Goan employees on payrolls:
If Goan employment is 60% or above, the entity receives 100% of the calculated benefit.
If Goan employment is more than 40% but less than 60%, the entity receives 80% of the calculated benefit.

Conditions
The entity must grant free access to any official authorized by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce for conducting inspection/supervision of the unit or the registers or holding discussions with the employed employees for ensuring proper utilization of the financial incentives/subsidies granted.
The entity must submit all necessary reports, information, and documents specified under the scheme or as required or directed by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce (DITC) time to time or as and when required.
The entity must ensure that the information and documents submitted are correct, otherwise, if found incorrect or false, the financial incentive shall be revoked.

Scheme Name: Information-Monitoring, Evaluation, and Social Audit (I-MESA): Social Audit
Nodal Ministry: Ministry Of Social Justice and Empowerment
Details: The scheme "Information, Monitoring, Evaluation and Social Audit (I-MESA)" was launched by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE), Govt. of India. The "Social Audit" component of the scheme aims to ensure that the implementation of the schemes at the ground level shall be examined intensely, ensuring transparency and accountability in the implementation of these programmes. The social audit process involves examining and assessing a programme/scheme with the active involvement of people, comparing official records with actual ground realities, and consolidating issues backed by evidence into a report. The scheme is implemented by Social Audit Units set up in every state under MGNREGA, facilitated by the National Resource Cell for Social Audits-DoSJE established at the National Institute of Social Defence, New Delhi.
Benefits:
Bringing to light gaps and lapses in programme implementation for improvement.
Creating awareness generation regarding the programmes being implemented.
Providing a platfm for mutual dialogue among various stakeholders for scheme improvement.
Providing a platform for right holders for timely grievance redressal.
Ensuring transparency and accountability in scheme implementation.
Seeking responses from primary stakeholders based on ground realities for course correction and policy framework impact.
Promoting people’s participation in all stages of programme implementation.
Conditions
The cost of conduct of social audits will be met from the respective scheme’s administrative cost.
Funds shall be given to Social Audit Units through the National Institute of Social Defence, New Delhi, based on budgets calculated and reviewed by the National Resource Cell for Social Audits.
The first installment (50% of the total budget) is provided after the submission of the social audit calendar.
The second tranche will be provided after completion of all audits, uploading of findings, and preparation of the annual analytical report.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must have experience of working with the Social Audit Unit for at least 2 to 3 years.
- The applicant must have experience facilitating social audits of schemes apart from the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
- The team Coordinator leading the team must preferably have completed a 30 days’ certificate course on social accountability and social audit.
- The applicant must ensure the representation of the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes community and the especially abled in the team.
- The team must preferably comprise 50% women members.

##### ***Desirable Criteria***

- The applicant should have experience working with the elderly, children, victims of substance abuse, and experience working in rehabilitative institutions.
- Anganwadi workers, Accredited Social Health Activists, Civil Society Organization representatives, or para-legal volunteers working in that area can be included in the team for community support and mobilization.
- Students/Interns from academic institutions can be engaged as members of the Social Justice Cell after being trained.

Scheme Name: Awas Sahayta Yojana for 100% Hearing and Visually Impaired Disabled Students in Special Trades of Industrial Training Institutes
Details: The scheme "Awas Sahayta Yojana for 100% Hearing and Visually Impaired Disabled Students in Special Trades of Industrial Training Institutes" was launched by the Department of Social Justice and Welfare for Persons with Disabilities, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The scheme aims to ensure qualitative admission of 100% hearing and visually impaired students equivalent to other categories, thereby enabling them to obtain high-quality technical education free from economic constraints. The scheme provides housing assistance and related allowances for food and accommodation to eligible disabled students pursuing specialized training programs in Industrial Training Institutes.
Benefits:
Housing assistance up to ₹4,000/- per student per month for food and accommodation is available, provided the student is studying outside their home residence at an Industrial Training Institute.
Housing assistance of ₹2,000/- per month per student for food and other expenses only is available, if the student receives hostel facility provided by the Principal of the Industrial Training Institute.
The assistance is provided for the academic duration of the training program, whether it is a one-year or two-year trade.
Disbursement
Mode:
 Funds are transferred using Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS).
Frequency:
 The sanctioned amount is transferred monthly into the student’s Aadhaar-based bank account. The Departmental District Officer provides the advance funds to the Principal of the Industrial Training Institute in two installments every six months.
Limit:
 The assistance is payable only once in a lifetime for the duration of the training program.
Geographic Scope:
 The scheme operates in 07 divisional Industrial Training Institutes located in Indore, Bhopal, Ujjain, Rewa, Jabalpur, Sagar, and Gwalior.
Conditions
The beneficiary disabled student must pay the rent amount to the landlord using an Account Payee Cheque.
The student must maintain regular attendance at the Industrial Training Institute for the Principal to disburse the monthly assistance amount.
Any rental amount exceeding the determined maximum housing assistance must be borne by the disabled students themselves from their own sources, and the department will provide no other facility.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be a student.


- The applicant must be 100% visually or hearing-impaired.
- The applicant must be admitted to an Industrial Training Institute.
- The applicant must not have received admission into any Government Hostel.
- The applicant must not have received assistance from any Government Department.

##### ***Post-Selection Conditions***
The applicant must present a certificate or declaration from the guardian stating that the guardian does not have an residential address at the same location or division where the Industrial Training Institute of regular study is situated.

Details: The scheme is implemented by the Government of Madhya Pradesh to benefit labourers residing in rural and agricultural sectors. 45 days’ wage equivalent for registered female workers or wives of registered workers (first two deliveries).
15 days’ wage equivalent for fathers (paternity leave).

Institutional deliveries covered under Janani Suraksha Yojana.
₹500/- aid for home deliveries of below-poverty-line women.
Managed by the Public Health & Family Welfare Department.

Coverage under Deendayal Antyodaya Upchar Yojana and State Illness Assistance Scheme.
Child heart-disease treatment under Mukhyamantri Bal Hriday Upchar Yojana.

Children of registered beneficiaries belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, or General Category will receive scholarships under respective departmental schemes.

Disabled children of registered workers with a disability of 40% or more will be eligible for disability scholarships.
Marriage Assistance –
Financial support for first marriage of registered workers’ daughters aged 18 + under Mukhyamantri Kanyadan/Nikah Yojana.

Normal death – ₹30,000/-
Accidental death – ₹75,000/-
Permanent disability – ₹75,000/-
Partial disability – ₹37,500/-
Funeral Assistance –

1. The applicant should be capable of performing wage labor.

Scheme Name: Gomantak Govsamvardhan Yojana
Details: The scheme "Gomantak Govsamvardhan Yojana" was launched by the Department of Animal Husbandry, Government of Goa. The scheme aims to conserve the Local Breeds of Cattle in the State of Goa by ensuring that Dairy Farmers or individuals rear these cattle, feeding them with feed, fodder, and providing water on a daily basis in their own property and cattle shed. The scheme provides financial assistance of ₹80/- per animal per day, disbursed quarterly, to cover maintenance costs including feed, fodder, and other miscellaneous costs, with a maximum limit of 05 Local Breed Cattle per family. The applications for this scheme are accepted by submitting a duly completed form along with a Notarized Agreement Bond to the relevant local area Assistant Director or Veterinary Officer.
Benefits:
Financial assistance of ₹80/- per animal per day.
This assistance covers the cost of maintenance of Local Breed Cattle, which includes feed, fodder, and other miscellaneous costs, bundled together in one component.
Microchipping or ear tagging of the cattle will be done by the area Assistant Director, Veterinary Officer, or Veterinary Assistant of the Veterinary Hospital/Dispensary sub-centres under the instruction of the Assistant Director or Veterinary Officer.
The subsidy will be credited in the account of the beneficiary.
Financial assistance will be provided on a quarterly basis.
The area Assistant Director or Veterinary Officer shall visit the cattle shed every month and submit the quarterly report (as per Annexure “A”) for the release of the subsidy.
Benefit Limitations
The Scheme will be limited for a maximum of total 05 Local Breed Cattle per family.
The Government has the power to restrict the number of cows to be reared per applicant.
The number of cattle to be reared shall be restricted to 250 cows per District for the Scheme in the financial year 2024-2025, with subsequent increases based on response.
Conditions
The beneficiary must ensure the cattle are stall-fed in the cattle shed or kept within the paddock area.
The cattle must be housed as per the approved housing regulations for cattle by the Bureau of Indian Standards.
The cattle must be housed in a fashion that can be easily inspected and counted by the local area Assistant Director or Veterinary Officer of the Department of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services.
The Local Breed Cattle must be regularly vaccinated. Refusal to vaccinate the cattle will lead to the forfeiture of the benefits of the scheme immediately, including any benefits supposed to be received.
If the Local Breeds Cattle are found let loose outside the paddock area, further benefit of the Scheme will be stopped immediately and the farmer will not be considered in the Scheme in the future.
One-Time Exemption: In case the animal has let itself loose due to circumstances beyond the control of the owner, only one chance will be given. This requires a written request providing photographic proof of the animals, duly recommended by the Area Officer, and addressed to the Director, Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must be a Dairy Farmer or an Individual of the State of Goa.
- The applicant must be a bonafide resident of Goa for at least the preceding 15 years.
- The applicant must own non-descript cattle or Shwet Kapila cattle.
- The applicant must have an adequate cattle shed as per the Bureau of Indian Standard.
- The scheme shall be applicable to rural areas and Class C and B Municipalities.
- The applicant must be responsible for fulfilling the Pollution Control Board norms if the number of cattle reared exceeds 25 in number.

_*If the number of applications received for rearing are more than 250 cattle per district, priority can be decided based on the grazing area of the beneficiary._
##### ***Reservation***

- Out of the 250 cattle per district, 12% shall be reserved for the Scheduled Tribes (ST).
- Out of the 250 cattle per district, 2% shall be reserved for the Scheduled Castes (SC) respectively.
- In case there is no demand in the reserved categories, the demand shall be booked under the general component.

Details: The scheme “Mukhyamantri Gramin Street Vendor Rin Yojana" was launched by the Department of Panchayat and Rural Development, Government of Madhya Pradesh. The loan is made available from banks following the training.
The benefit is only for existing businesses (old enterprises) in the rural area.
The benefit is for establishing new businesses for migrant workers.
Rural migrant workers establishing a new business must undergo Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP) training through Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETI).

- The applicant must reside in Madhya Pradesh.
- The applicant must reside in a rural area.
- The applicant must be between 18 and 55 years of age.
- The applicant must belong to the poor class.
- The applicant must be a migrant worker or a small trader (Street Vendor).
- The applicant must be applying for a loan for an existing enterprise located in a rural area.
- The applicant must be a migrant worker establishing a new enterprise.

Scheme Name: Mukhyamantri Saur Swarojgar Yojana - Uttarakhand Renewable Energy Development Agency
Details: The scheme “Mukhyamantri Saur Swarojgar Yojana” is implemented by the Uttarakhand Renewable Energy Development Agency (UREDA) under the Department of Energy, Government of Uttarakhand. The scheme aims to promote self-employment among the residents of Uttarakhand by enabling them to establish and operate solar power projects, thereby generating clean energy, providing a sustainable source of income, and encouraging entrepreneurship.
Benefits:
Under the scheme, self-employment is provided to eligible applicants/beneficiaries through the allocation of solar power projects with capacities of 20, 25, 50, 100, and 200 kW, as detailed below:
20 kW: Project cost ₹10 lakh; land required – 300 sq. meters.
25 kW: Project cost ₹12.50 lakh; land required – 300 sq. meters.
50 kW: Project cost ₹25.00 lakh; land required – 700–1000 sq. meters.
100 kW: Project cost ₹50.00 lakh; land required – 1500–2000 sq. meters.
200 kW: Project cost ₹100.00 lakh; land required – 3000–4000 sq. meters.
(Selected candidates will be provided loans from Uttarakhand State/District Cooperative Banks at an interest rate of 8%. Additionally, beneficiaries will be eligible for incentives and benefits under the MSME Policy-2023, provided by the Industries Department.)
The electricity generated from the allotted solar projects will be purchased by Uttarakhand Power Corporation Limited (UPCL) for a period of 25 years. Payments to beneficiaries will be made according to the prevailing tariff rates for the electricity sold.
Eligibility Criteria:
1. The applicant must be a permanent resident of Uttarakhand.
   1. Only one solar power plant will be allotted per family, and each applicant is eligible for only one project.
   1. To avail benefits under the current MSME Policy, the allottee must apply under this scheme as a proprietorship. Applications in the form of a partnership firm, company, trust, or society will not be permitted.

Scheme Name: Interest Subsidy Scheme, 2017
Details: The scheme "Interest Subsidy Scheme, 2017” was launched by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce (DITC), Government of Goa. The scheme aims to incentivize units for making their enterprises financially viable. The scheme provides interest subsidy on term loan and/or working capital loan availed from specified financial institutions. The subsidy is subject to minimum engagement of 60% Goan manpower, with maximum benefits up to ₹25,00,000/- per annum (or ₹27,50,000/- for all women and Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe applicants).
Benefits:
For claims of interest paid on term loan, subsidy will be calculated to the extent of 30% of the interest paid, subject to the scheme ceiling.
For claims of interest paid on working capital loan, subsidy will be calculated to the extent of 1½% of the total turnover or 30% of the interest paid by the units/enterprise, whichever is less.
The subsidy payable shall not exceed the ceiling of ₹25,00,000/- per annum, calculated on pro-rata basis for part of the year as claimed.
The subsidy payable shall not exceed the ceiling of ₹27,50,000/- per annum for all women and Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe applicants, calculated on pro-rata basis for part of the year as claimed.
Disbursal Conditions/Criteria
The period of grant of subsidy shall not exceed seven years, that is 27 continuous quarters subsequent to the quarter in which the subsidy is first claimed.
The benefits under this scheme shall be disbursed to eligible applicants beyond the validity of this scheme, provided, application for at least one claim is submitted to the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce (DITC) during the validity of this scheme.
In case the unit fails to file the yearly claim after the first claim within the stipulated time frame, the unit shall be eligible to file the delayed claim in the subsequent year within the time frame as specified in the Umbrella Scheme.
The facility of filing delayed claims shall not be available for the last claim.
The lapsed claim shall not be revived by any authority.
In case the unit fails to include any portion of interest that cannot be claimed due to non-payment before filing of application, the unit shall be eligible to claim such interest subject to payment of the same in the subsequent year.
In case of default in payment of term loan (i.e. not paid as per schedule of repayment) reimbursement of interest shall be reduced to the extent of default.
Only the limit of original loan granted and not rescheduled loan shall be considered for interest reimbursement.
Eligibility Criteria:
- The applicant must represent one of the following - 

             (a)   A Micro, Small and Medium manufacturing industry.
             (b)   A project of Hinterland Eco tourism in lesser developed talukas registered with/recognized by the Department of Tourism/Goa Investment Promotion Board/Town & Country Planning/Planning & Development Authority/Eco Sensitive Zone Authority.

- The industry must be listed under White category, Green category and Orange category.
- The industry must have commenced production after 01-10-2017.
- The industry must engage a minimum of 60% of Goan manpower on regular employment.
- The industry must have availed loan as term loan and/or working capital loan for conducting business of the unit claiming the benefit.
- The loan must be availed from any nationalized bank, scheduled private bank, Co-operative Bank, Economic Development Corporation Limited, or any Non-Banking Financial Institutions recognized by the Reserve Bank of India.

Scheme Name: Incentives to Green Investment Scheme
Details: The “Incentives to Green Investment Scheme” was launched by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce (DITC), Government of Goa. The scheme aims to give financial support to industrial units for adopting environmentally friendly equipment and processes, and to support the adoption of new technology and renewable energy aimed at conserving the use of natural resources. Water and Energy Audit Reimbursement
Reimbursement of 25% of the cost of water and energy audits.
Subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000/- per unit during the validity of this scheme.
Energy Conservation Equipment Capital Reimbursement
Reimbursement of 40% of the capital cost incurred on the purchase of the equipment.
Subject to ₹10,00,000/- per unit.
A unit can avail this benefit multiple times, subject to the maximum ceiling mentioned above.
This benefit shall be in addition to benefits availed under State and Central Subsidy Schemes.
Maximum Benefit Cap Conditions
The total subsidy received by the applicant towards the purchase of the said equipment must not exceed 100% of the purchase value of the respective equipment.
For the purpose of calculation, total subsidy includes: Subsidy under this scheme + Any other Subsidy received from Government of Goa/Government of India + Interest subsidy received/receivable under any soft loan or low interest loan availed for purchasing the said equipment under any State/Central Government scheme.
Benchmark interest for calculating interest subsidy as received due to a subsidized rate of interest will be 10%.
Conditions
The benefits under this scheme are subject to budgetary allocation.
No Promissory Estoppel shall be applicable if benefits are discontinued because allocation is exceeded.
The applicant must allow and/or grant free access to any official authorized by the Directorate of Industries, Trade and Commerce for conducting inspection/supervision of the unit or registers or holding discussions with employed employees for ensuring proper utilization of the financial incentives/subsidies granted by the State Government.

- The applicant must be a manufacturing unit.
- The applicant must fall under the micro, small, medium, or large category.
- The applicant must ensure the water and energy audits, if claimed, are carried out by a recognised institution/consultant certified by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Ministry of Power and Government of India.
